title: DMA (Direct Memory Access) controller
summary: A DMA controller transfers data between memory and peripherals without CPU involvement. The CPU programs the DMA controller with: source address, destination address, transfer count, transfer mode (single, block, demand, cascade), and direction (memory-to-memory, memory-to-I/O, I/O-to-memory). The DMA controller then performs the transfer and interrupts the CPU on completion.

structure.meaning: Starting address of the source (memory or I/O port).
Starting address of the destination (memory or I/O port).
Transfer mode (single, block, demand, cascade), direction (read/write/verify), auto-initialize, address increment/decrement.
Terminal count, request, service, and channel status bits.
Enable/disable DMA, memory-to-memory, controller priority, timing, etc.

notes: DMA frees the CPU to do other work during data transfers.
Modern systems use bus-mastering DMA (device initiates transfer) instead of a separate DMA controller.
DMA is essential for high-throughput I/O (disk, network, audio).
IOMMU (I/O Memory Management Unit) provides address translation and protection for DMA.
